beats.text: King Janaka of Mithila welcomed the princes with honor. He was a king and a sage at once, wise and gentle.
In his palace lay Shiva's mighty bow, so heavy that it took hundreds of men to pull it on its eight-wheeled cart. Not even gods and demons could lift it.
Many kings had come for it. Not one could even raise it off the ground.
Janaka had made a vow: whoever strings this bow will marry my daughter, Sita.
Vishwamitra turned to Rama and smiled. He knew exactly why he had brought Rama here.
Rama looked at the bow and said quietly, 'May I touch it?' Janaka nodded, and the whole court held its breath.
Now the great box was opened. Rama stepped closer, and the whole hall fell silent.
